headline: State Campground and Island Use Permits
reservation: New York State DEC manages most island camping and public beaches, requiring reservations months in advance for peak summer. Distinguish between mainland hotel bookings and specific permits needed for island day-use or dockage. Verify current site requirements through official DEC portals.

days.title: Village Waterfront and Beach
days.start: Suggested: 9:30 AM from Lake George Village

stops.name: Shepard Park
stops.detail: Walk the southern basin waterfront to orient yourself with the lake's scale.

stops.name: Million Dollar Beach
stops.detail: Visit this state-managed beach for swimming and lakeside relaxation.

days.note: Parking at Million Dollar Beach is limited; arrive early during summer holidays.

days.title: Mountain Views and History

stops.name: Prospect Mountain
stops.detail: Hike the challenging trail or drive the seasonal highway for panoramic summit views.

stops.name: Fort William Henry
stops.detail: Explore the reconstructed 18th-century fort to learn about regional colonial history.

days.driving: Allow 30 minutes; conditions vary by mode
days.note: Check seasonal road opening dates for the Prospect Mountain Veterans Memorial Highway.

days.title: Adirondack Slopes and Trails

stops.name: Buck Mountain
stops.detail: Summit this eastern-shore peak for rewarding views of the lake's many islands.

stops.name: Lake George Battlefield State Park
stops.detail: Walk the historic grounds to see monuments from the French and Indian War.

days.driving: Allow 1 hour; conditions vary on Route 9N
days.note: Buck Mountain requires sturdy footwear for uneven terrain and significant elevation.

intel.title: Village Congestion
intel.text: Street parking in Lake George Village is often metered and limited during summer weekends. Utilize designated public lots or stay within walking distance to avoid delays.

intel.title: Highland Reception
intel.text: Cell service is generally reliable in the village but often fails on the slopes of Buck Mountain. Download offline trail maps for any Adirondack hiking.

intel.title: Village Services
intel.text: Fuel and supplies are abundant in Lake George Village and Glens Falls. Services become much sparser as you drive north toward Ticonderoga.

intel.title: Hiking Seasons
intel.text: Spring trails can be muddy and prone to erosion; early fall offers peak foliage views without the summer heat. Some attractions reduce hours after Labor Day.

intel.title: Water Navigation
intel.text: Boaters must follow specific Lake George Park Commission regulations regarding invasive species and speed. Ensure your vessel is registered and inspected before launching.

plan.arrival: Pick up rental at Rutland (RUT) and drive approximately 65 minutes to Lake George Village for orientation.
plan.vehicle: Standard vehicles are suitable for main roads; some trailhead access may be easier with higher clearance.
plan.goldenHour: Sunset from the summit of Prospect Mountain; check highway closure times for evening access.
